Tooling specifications and clients SHOULD use the openapi field to interpret the OpenAPI document.
Each Parameter Object MUST contain either a schema property or a content property, but MUST NOT contain both.
When a Schema Object sets nullable to true, that Schema Object MUST explicitly define a type so that null can be added to the allowed type.
The major.minor portion of the semantic version number SHALL designate the OAS feature set.

All platform service OpenAPI documents MUST define the enterprise observability metadata as OpenAPI Specification Extension fields named exactly monitor.sla, monitor.owner, and monitor.tier. These field names are hardcoded in the observability platform's schema parser and MUST NOT be changed.

Each new minor version of the OpenAPI Specification SHALL allow any OpenAPI document that is valid against a previous minor version within the same major version to be updated to the new Specification version with equivalent semantics, and that update MUST only require changing the openapi property to the new minor version.
OpenAPI documents that provide an Info Object termsOfService field MUST encode that field as a Markdown string.
When users divide an OpenAPI document into multiple connected parts, they MUST use $ref fields in the specification to reference those parts.
When an Operation Object defines a requestBody for an HTTP GET method, consumers MUST process and transmit that requestBody as the structured query payload.
An OpenAPI document that conforms to the OpenAPI Specification MAY be represented in either JSON or YAML format.
All field names in the OpenAPI Specification are case sensitive unless the specification explicitly states that certain keys are case insensitive.
OpenAPI path templates MUST use curly braces ({}) to delimit replaceable URL path segments.
When a Security Requirement Object contains multiple schemes, a request SHALL be authorized if any one of those schemes is successfully validated.

OpenAPI documents MUST include the Info Object title field and the Info Object version field.

All Operations MUST include the extension field x-category for annotating business domain classification; all Operations MUST also include the extension field x-category for annotating security audit classification.
OpenAPI documents that provide an Info Object termsOfService field MUST encode that field as a URL.
The version field in the Info Object MUST reflect the current deployed version of the API implementation, and MUST be updated whenever a new version of the API is released to production.
The Info Object version field MUST represent the version of the OpenAPI document rather than the OpenAPI Specification version or the API implementation version.
OpenAPI descriptions MAY use CommonMark syntax for rich text representation.

OpenAPI path templates MUST use curly braces ({}) to delimit replaceable URL path segments.
OpenAPI documents MUST NOT define templated paths with the same hierarchy but different templated names because such paths are identical.
Each Operation Object MUST include a responses field that lists the possible responses returned by executing that operation.

When an API parameter is renamed between versions, the corresponding Path Item Object or Operation Object MUST include both the original parameter declaration and the renamed parameter declaration during the transition period, and both declarations MUST use the same name at the same location, so that existing clients require no modification to remain functional.
Each Parameter Object MUST include both a name field and an in field.
OpenAPI documents that provide an Info Object termsOfService field MUST encode that field as plain text.
OpenAPI documents that provide an Info Object termsOfService field MUST NOT encode that field as plain text.
Path Item Objects and Operation Objects MUST NOT include duplicated parameters; a unique parameter is defined by the combination of its name and location.
OpenAPI documents that provide an Info Object termsOfService field MUST encode that field as a Markdown string.
Each field name in the Paths Object MUST begin with a backslash (\).
Parameter Objects MUST set the in field to one of the following values: query, header, path, or cookie.
When a Parameter Object sets in to path its name field MUST correspond to a template expression that occurs within the associated path.
When a Schema Object uses allOf, oneOf, or anyOf, each inline or referenced schema in those arrays MUST be a Schema Object rather than a standard JSON Schema.

Each Operation Object MUST define at least one response.

Each Response Object MUST include a description field.
Each field name in the Paths Object MUST begin with a backslash (\).
Each Security Scheme Object MUST include a type field.
Security Scheme Objects MUST set the type field to one of the following values: apiKey, http, oauth2, or openIdConnect.
Authors MAY use the default response object as the default response for all HTTP status codes that are not covered individually.
Each Security Scheme Object whose type is oauth2 MUST include a flows object containing configuration information for the supported flow types.

Patterned fields MUST have unique names within their containing object.
Each tag name in the OpenAPI Object tags list MUST be unique.
When an Operation Object defines requestBody for an HTTP method whose request-body semantics are vague in the HTTP specification, consumers SHALL ignore that requestBody.
Each field name in the Paths Object MUST begin with an alphanumeric character.

Parameters defined at the Path Item level MAY be overridden at the Operation level but MUST NOT be removed there.
